explainedBy: Dracula depends on sleeping in the consecrated soil of his earth boxes to maintain his power
Dracula distributes the earth boxes across London using human logistics to create safe houses
The investigators audit Dracula and exploit the paper trail left by his bureaucracy
Jonathan Harker follows the paper trail to identify the delivery carters who moved Dracula's boxes

storyboard.claim: The investigators trace the physical movers who transported Dracula's boxes across London.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jonathan Harker stands on a London street reviewing delivery manifests of the carters.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the concept of auditing Dracula to tracing the specific delivery carters.
storyboard.addedInformation: Grounds the investigation in physical London legwork and handwritten receipts.

explainedBy: Carter Patterson operated as a massive commercial parcel moving firm in London
Harker and Seward inspect the carrier's messy, dog-eared notebook filled with thick pencil entries

storyboard.claim: The investigators inspect the carter's messy, dog-eared delivery notebook.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the delivery company to the physical notebook containing the movement records.

explainedBy: The heroes decipher the notebook and trace Dracula's earth boxes to a massive house in Piccadilly
Jonathan Harker investigates property records in Piccadilly and uncovers Dracula's alias Count Deville
The hunters sterilize Dracula's earth boxes by placing pieces of the sacred host inside them
Dr. Seward documents their campaign to liquidate Dracula's assets by sterilizing the earth boxes
The systematic sterilization of safe houses strips Dracula of refuge and catches him at his weakest
Dracula believed he had built an unassailable structure by decentralizing his hiding places
Van Helsing notes that Dracula adapts and experiments after the paper trail proves fatal
Dracula attempts to move the last boxes himself but the shipping invoice has already doomed him

storyboard.claim: While the data tracking proceeds, a dark parallel subplot unfolds in the asylum.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitions from the bureaucratic audit of Dracula to the parallel asylum subplot.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the upcoming Renfield narrative as a thematic mirror to the geopolitical logistics.

explainedBy: Dracula is introduced in the parallel comparison as a towering dark figure sweeping into a room

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the side-by-side comparison with the grand supernatural horror.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes Dracula's overwhelming physical scale before showing his pathetic mirror.

explainedBy: Renfield mirrors Dracula's predatory nature from the opposite end as a tiny, insignificant insect-catcher

storyboard.claim: On the opposing side stands an insignificant human mirror of the vampire.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A close-up of Renfield in his rumpled grey asylum jacket reaching nervously into the corner.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cuts to the opposite side of the comparison: the pathetic asylum inmate.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts Renfield's cramped vulnerability against Dracula's aristocratic power.

explainedBy: The cosmic horror of Dracula is mirrored in the clinical obsession of asylum patient Renfield
Dr. Seward's lunatic asylum borders the Carfax estate that Dracula bought
Carfax is strategically located beside the asylum where Renfield consumes living flies
Renfield uses captive flies to catch spiders to consume greater life force

storyboard.claim: Renfield uses captive flies to catch spiders to consume greater life force.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Renfield sits on the floor of his asylum room with a manic smirk, trapping spiders.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From eating flies to escalating his predation toward larger organisms.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the escalating ladder of Renfield's zoophagous method in his room.

explainedBy: Dr. Seward classifies Renfield's escalating predation as zoophagous mania

storyboard.claim: Dr. Seward classifies Renfield's escalating predation as zoophagous mania.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dr. Seward observes Renfield slumped on the asylum bench while taking clinical diagnosis notes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Renfield's bird-eating ambitions to Dr. Seward's medical classification.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces Seward's clinical perspective attempting to categorize Renfield's behavior.

explainedBy: Seward records that Renfield desires to absorb as many lives as possible in a cumulative way
Renfield builds a pyramid scheme of consumed lives to prolong his own existence indefinitely

storyboard.claim: Renfield constructs a pyramid scheme of life force to prolong his own existence.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Seward's diary observation to the structural logic of Renfield's life-force pyramid.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visualizes the cumulative ladder of consumption Renfield believes will grant him longevity.

explainedBy: Renfield's consumption of insects forms a microeconomy mirroring Dracula's accumulation of blood
Dracula sustains immortality through macro predation while Renfield feeds on small insects
Renfield quotes scripture to Seward that the blood is the life, revealing their parasitic nature
Dracula uses Renfield not merely as a thematic mirror but as a tactical pawn in his invasion
A vampire cannot enter Seward's asylum without first being invited by an inmate or resident
Mina Harker is sheltered inside the asylum while Dracula requires a legal invitation to breach it

storyboard.claim: Dracula appears at Renfield's cell window, exploiting his mental fragility with promises of lives.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the rule requiring an invitation to Dracula's direct psychological manipulation at the window.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visualizes the sinister predatory transaction through the physical cell bars.

explainedBy: Renfield is overwhelmed by Dracula's promise of life force and collapses to worship the vampire

storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Dracula's tempting offers to Renfield's complete psychological and physical collapse.

explainedBy: Renfield opens the window sash and invites Dracula inside, saying 'come in, lord and master'

storyboard.addedInformation: Captures the exact fateful moment of speech breaking the asylum's legal threshold.

explainedBy: Dracula gains legal invited entrance into the asylum by breaching its weakest link

storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Dracula's physical entry to the intellectual critique of Victorian medical science.

explainedBy: Dr. Seward observes and analyzes Renfield daily, compiling extensive clinical notes in his diary
Seward believes he is studying madness while oblivious to Dracula manipulating his patient right under his nose

explainedBy: The scientific method fails because Victorian medicine refuses to account for the irrational

storyboard.concreteVisual: Dr. Seward sits slumped beside the scales of justice and reason in his dim library.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Articulates the philosophical failure of pure rationalism against gothic horror.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Seward defeated by the limitations of his scientific training.

explainedBy: Seward remains locked in his medical paradigm, blind to Dracula standing outside the window
